item.title: Melting Arctic ice allows large whales to move in 北极海冰融化，大型鲸类得以进入新海域
item.description:
东格陵兰的海冰持续消融，使得巨型鲸类得以利用这一机遇，进入此前无法涉足的海域。

The sea off the coast of East Greenland used to be covered in ice year-round. Now, as it warms and melts completely in the summer, the waters have opened up to new visitors – some of the world's largest whales and the fish that they feed on.

东格陵兰沿岸海域过去全年都被海冰覆盖。现在，随着海水变暖，海冰会在夏季完全融化，这片水域也因此迎来新的 “访客”，包括世界上一些体型最大的鲸类及其捕食的鱼类。

The scientists combined aerial surveys, satellite tagging and observations from local Inuit communities to track them. And the change has been dramatic.

科学家通过结合航空调查、卫星标签定位以及当地因纽特社区的观测，对这些鲸类展开追踪。而其变化十分显著。

Surveys didn't record a single humpback whale sighting in the region until 2006. In 2007, seven humpbacks were seen. And, by 2024, there were 150 sightings of the giant whales from ships. Now, fin whales, humpbacks and minke whales come to East Greenland in their thousands to feed.

直到 2006 年，相关调查才首次在该地区记录到座头鲸的目击报告。2007 年，有七头座头鲸被目击。而到了 2024 年，船只目击这种巨型鲸类的记录已达 150 次。如今，成千上万的长须鲸、座头鲸和小须鲸会汇聚到东格陵兰觅食。

The researchers say this is a huge climate-driven shift, with some easily adapting, while other Arctic species, including belugas, narwhals and walruses, all of which need the ice to hide from predators or to breed, are being edged out.

研究人员表示，这是一次由气候变化驱动的巨大转变。一些物种能够轻松适应，而另一些极地物种，包括白鲸、独角鲸和海象，因需要依赖海冰躲避天敌或繁育后代，正逐渐失去生存空间。

词汇表

year-round 全年
melts 融化
aerial 空中的，航空的
tagging 标记追踪
Inuit 因纽特人的
humpback 座头鲸
sighting 发现记录，目击记录
fin 鳍
minke 小须鲸
shift 变化，转变
belugas 白鲸
narwhals 独角鲸
walruses 海象
predators 捕食者
breed 繁殖
edge out 逐渐取代，排挤

听力练习（答案见下页）

一、听第一遍音频，回答问题。

1. Is this article mainly about…
a. new food sources for whales.
b. new whale migration patterns.

二、用一分钟阅读下列问题，然后听第二遍音频并回答问题。

1. The ocean near East Greenland is covered with ice all year round.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

2. There is nothing for whales to eat in these new ocean regions.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

3. As well as technology, scientists spoke to local people.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

4. Humpback whales were first seen in East Greenland in _______.
a. 2006
b. 2007
c. 2024

5. The opening up of this area of sea has also been positive for belugas, narwhals and walruses.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、听第三遍音频，将句子补充完整。（提示：可以反复听，直到听清楚每一个词）

1. The ______________ coast of East Greenland used to be covered in ice year-round.

2. Surveys didn't ______________ humpback whale sighting in the region until 2006. 

答案

一、听第一遍音频，回答问题。

b. The article mentions food and feeding, but is mainly about new migration patterns, as more areas of sea are opened up by melting ice.

二、用一分钟阅读下列问题，然后听第二遍音频并回答问题。

1. b. False. The sea off the coast of East Greenland used to be covered in ice year-round. Now, as it warms and melts completely in the summer, the waters have opened up to new visitors - some of the world's largest whales and the fish that they feed on.

2. b. False. The sea off the coast of East Greenland used to be covered in ice year-round. Now, as it warms and melts completely in the summer, the waters have opened up to new visitors - some of the world's largest whales and the fish that they feed on.

3. a. True. The scientists combined aerial surveys, satellite tagging and observations from local Inuit communities to track them.

4. a. Surveys didn't record a single humpback whale sighting in the region until 2006.

5. b. False. The researchers say this is a huge climate-driven shift, with some easily adapting, while other Arctic species, including belugas, narwhals and walruses, all of which need the ice to hide from predators or to breed, are being edged out.

三、听第三遍音频，将句子补充完整。（提示：可以反复听，直到听清楚每一个词）

1. The sea off the coast of East Greenland used to be covered in ice year-round.

2. Surveys didn't record a single humpback whale sighting in the region until 2006.

item.title: Huge Roman villa found under popular park dubbed town's 'Pompeii' 小镇热门公园地下发现罗马别墅遗址，被誉为当地的 “庞贝古城”
item.description:
考古学家发现了迄今在威尔士发现的最大罗马别墅遗址。他们认为这一 “了不起的发现” 有望成为 “塔尔博特港的庞贝古城”。

Beloved by generations of visitors and steeped in history, Margam Park was already known to have an Iron Age hill fort, the remains of a Norman abbey and a Victorian castle, which looks out today over Port Talbot steelworks. Now, though, it can add a Roman villa to that list.

马格姆公园深受几代访客喜爱，且历史底蕴深厚。这里原本就因拥有一座铁器时代的山丘堡垒、一处诺曼时期修道院遗址，以及一座俯瞰塔尔博特港钢铁厂的维多利亚时期的城堡而闻名。而现在，公园的古迹名单上又多了一座罗马别墅遗址。

Sophisticated scanning devices were used to look for archaeological features hidden underground, and the Swansea University-led team struck gold.

由斯旺西大学领衔的团队利用先进的扫描设备寻找埋藏在地下的考古遗迹，并取得了这一重大发现。

The villa itself has multiple rooms, a substantial side building, and it sits within a defensive enclosure. The experts hope to find mosaic floors and other precious artefacts, and say their discovery is of a scale and level of preservation unmatched in Wales so far.

这座别墅拥有多个房间、一座规模颇大的附属建筑，并坐落于一处设有防御设施的围合区域内。专家希望在此发现马赛克地面和其它珍贵文物，并表示，无论是遗址规模还是保存状况，此次发现在威尔士都堪称首屈一指。

词汇表

beloved 深受喜爱的，备受喜爱的
steeped 浸润于…中的，有着深厚…底蕴的
Iron Age 铁器时代
hill fort 山丘堡垒
abbey 修道院
steelworks 钢铁厂
scanning 扫描用的
struck gold 取得重大发现
mosaic 马赛克
unmatched 首屈一指的，无与伦比的

听力练习

一、听第一遍音频，回答问题。

1.The Roman villa was found…
a. after years of searching for it. 
b. on a site that already has historical remains.  
c. accidentally by visitors of Margam Park. 

二、用一分钟阅读下列问题，然后听第二遍音频并回答问题。

1. From a Victorian castle on the site, you can see…
a. the Roman villa. 
b. Port Talbot steelworks. 
c. Swansea University.

2. Researchers found gold on the site of the villa. 
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

3. What surrounds the Roman villa?
a. a defensive enclosure
b. multiple rooms
c. one large side building

4. Researchers founda mosaic floor in the villa.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

5. Which word best describes the scale and level of preservation of the villa compared to others found in Wales?
a. unconventional
b. uncertain
c. unparalleled

三、听第三遍音频，将句子补充完整。（提示：可以反复听，直到听清楚每一个词）

1. Margam Park was already known ______________ Iron Age hill fort.

2. Sophisticated scanning devices were used to look for archaeological features ______________.

答案

一、听第一遍音频，回答问题。

b. Beloved by generations of visitors and steeped in history, Margam Park was already known to have an Iron Age hill fort, the remains of a Norman abbey and a Victorian castle.

二、用一分钟阅读下列问题，然后听第二遍音频并回答问题。

1. b. …and a Victorian castle, which looks out today over Port Talbot steelworks. 

2. c. Not given. …the Swansea University-led team struck gold. The phrase 'struck gold' is metaphorical, not literal. It is not mentioned whether gold was found.

3. a. The villa itself has multiple rooms, a substantial side building and it sits within a defensive enclosure.  

4. b. False. The experts hope to find mosaic floors and other precious artefacts…

5. c. …and say their discovery is of a scale and level of preservation unmatched in Wales so far.

三、听第三遍音频，将句子补充完整。（提示：可以反复听，直到听清楚每一个词）

1. Margam Park was already known to have an Iron Age hill fort.

2. Sophisticated scanning devices were used to look for archaeological features hidden underground.

item.title: Spider monkeys sharing fruit knowledge 蜘蛛猴分享果树情报
item.description:
你是否问过朋友 “你的零食看起来挺好吃，是从哪买的”？一个研究团队发现，蜘蛛猴其实也会互相分享这种 “内部情报”，告诉同伴哪里能找到最好吃的果树。

Researchers from universities in Edinburgh and Mexico spent seven years studying the behaviour of black-handed spider monkeys in the Yucatan Peninsula. They observed that the large groups the primates live in split into smaller subgroups when searching for food. Different combinations of monkeys would split off each time, meaning the same subgroup might never forage together twice.

来自爱丁堡和墨西哥多所大学的研究人员花了七年时间研究尤卡坦半岛上黑掌蜘蛛猴的行为。他们观察到，这类灵长目动物群居的大群体会在寻找食物时分成一个个小分队。每次分出来的小分队成员都不同，这意味着几乎不会出现原班人马第二次一起觅食的情况。

Dr Matthew Silk from the University of Edinburgh says these groups are a clever way of sharing knowledge about the locations of the best fruit trees. Some parts of the forest were known by many monkeys, like a town's favourite restaurant, while others were known by just one or two, like a hidden gem.

爱丁堡大学的马修·西尔克博士称，这种分组方式很聪明，可以有效地分享最好吃的果树位置。森林里的某些地方就像城里最受欢迎的餐厅，很多猴子都知道；而有些地方则像一个鲜为人知的 “宝藏小店”，只有一两只猴子了解。

词汇表

black-handed 黑色手掌的
peninsula 半岛
observed 观察到
primates 灵长目动物
subgroups 子群，子组
split off 分离
forage 觅食
hidden gem 隐藏的宝石，非常美好但鲜为人知的东西

听力练习

一、听第一遍音频，回答问题。

1. Do spider monkeys work together or individually to find food?

二、用一分钟阅读下列问题，然后听第二遍音频并回答问题。

1. Researchers spent seven months studying black-handed spider monkeys.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

2. Spider monkeys are usually in large groups.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

3. Spider monkeys always search for food with the same partners.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

4. Spider monkeys share their knowledge of the best fruit trees…
a. by talking to each other.
b. by working in different groups.
c. by hiding gems.

三、听第三遍音频，将句子补充完整。（提示：可以反复听，直到听清楚每一个词）

1. Different combinations of monkeys would ______________ time, meaning the same subgroup might never forage together twice.

2. Some parts of the forest were known by many monkeys, like a town's favourite restaurant, while others were known by just one or two, like ______________.

答案

一、听第一遍音频，回答问题。

1. Spider monkeys work in groups to find the best fruit trees.

二、用一分钟阅读下列问题，然后听第二遍音频并回答问题。

1. b. False. Researchers from universities in Edinburgh and Mexico spent seven years studying the behaviour of black-handed spider monkeys in the Yucatan Peninsula.

2. a. True. They observed that the large groups the primates live in split into smaller subgroups when searching for food.

3. b. False. Different combinations of monkeys would split off each time, meaning the same subgroup might never forage together twice.

4. b. Dr Matthew Silk from the University of Edinburgh says these groups are a clever way of sharing knowledge about the locations of the best fruit trees.

三、听第三遍音频，将句子补充完整。（提示：可以反复听，直到听清楚每一个词）

1. Different combinations of monkeys would split off each time, meaning the same subgroup might never forage together twice.

2. Some parts of the forest were known by many monkeys, like a town's favourite restaurant, while others were known by just one or two, like a hidden gem.

item.title: Near-extinct snails rescued from rock 濒临灭绝的蜗牛从岩缝中获救
item.description:
英国动物园的保育人员成功繁育出 300 只濒临灭绝的小型蜗牛，并将它们重新放归野外。

Less than a centimetre in size, these tiny snails had been pushed to the brink of extinction.

这些体长不足一厘米的小型蜗牛一度濒临灭绝。

Their home on the Madeira Archipelago had been grazed bare by invasive goats and rabbits, while mice saw the molluscs as a water source.

它们在马德拉群岛上的栖息地被入侵的山羊和兔子啃食殆尽，而老鼠则将这些软体动物当作水分的来源。

But after conservation work, including a breeding programme at Chester Zoo, hundreds of the snails have now been returned to the wild. The team said they had one shot to save the species.

不过，在实施了一系列动物保护措施后，包括切斯特动物园的一个繁育项目，数百只蜗牛如今已经被重新放归野外。研究团队表示，他们只有这一次机会来拯救这一物种。

The mission involved transporting them in the dark to snail-friendly crevices in the rocks. It's hoped they come out of their shell to restore soil and boost the natural habitat.

此次行动包括在夜间将这些蜗牛转移到适宜生存的岩石缝中。人们希望它们能从壳中爬出、重新活跃起来，从而帮助恢复土壤环境，促进当地生态栖息地的恢复。

词汇表

centimetre 厘米
tiny 极小的，微小的
brink 边缘
extinction 灭绝
grazed （牲畜）吃草，啃过了
invasive 入侵的，外来的
molluscs 软体动物
breeding 繁育，繁殖
one shot （仅有的）一次机会
crevices 缝隙，裂隙
restore 恢复
boost 促进，改善

听力练习

一、听第一遍音频，回答问题。

1. What are the hopes for the conservation project?

二、用一分钟阅读下列问题，然后听第二遍音频并回答问题。

1. The snails are more than one centimetre long.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

2. Which reason for the snails' near-extinction is true?
a. Their habitat was damaged by invasive animals.
b. They could not find enough sunlight.
c. They struggled to find a water source.

3. What role did Chester Zoo play in the conservation effort?
a. It ran a breeding programme for the snails.
b. It removed all the rabbits from the archipelago.
c. It transported the snails to the islands.

4. The snails were transported during the day to help them adjust to sunlight.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

5. Scientists are certain that the snail population will double within the next year.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、听第三遍音频，将句子补充完整。（提示：可以反复听，直到听清楚每一个词）

1. Less than a centimetre in size, these tiny snails had been ______________ the brink of extinction.

2. The team said they had ______________ to save the species.

答案

一、听第一遍音频，回答问题。

It's hoped the snails will come out of their shell to restore soil and boost the natural habitat.

二、用一分钟阅读下列问题，然后听第二遍音频并回答问题。

1. b. False. Less than a centimetre in size, these tiny snails had been pushed to the brink of extinction.

2. a. Their home on the Madeira Archipelago had been grazed bare by invasive goats and rabbits, while mice saw the molluscs as a water source.

3. a. But after conservation work, including a breeding program at Chester Zoo, hundreds of the snails have now been returned to the wild.

4. b. False. The mission involved transporting them in the dark to snail-friendly crevices in the rock.

5. c. Not given. The text mentions hopes for environmental benefits, but it does not mention the population doubling or any future population estimates.

三、听第三遍音频，将句子补充完整。（提示：可以反复听，直到听清楚每一个词）

1. Less than a centimetre in size, these tiny snails had been pushed to the brink of extinction.

2. The team said they had one shot to save the species.

item.title: Chimpanzees build trust through touch 黑猩猩通过肢体接触建立信任
item.description:
一些科学家在研究和我们亲缘关系最近的类人猿后发现，在面临压力事件之前进行肢体接触、拥抱和亲吻，可能是一种古老的建立信任的方式。

Anyone who watches team sports may be familiar with the sight of players joining a huddle before a big match. Researchers studying chimpanzees and bonobos in African sanctuaries found our closest ape relatives do something similar before feeding time, one of the most competitive moments in their day.

经常观看团队体育比赛的人，对赛前队员们围成一圈加油打气的场景应该不会陌生。在非洲多家灵长类动物保护区研究黑猩猩和倭黑猩猩的科研人员们发现，这些与人类亲缘关系最近的类人猿在喂食时间前也会有类似的举动。喂食时间是它们一天中竞争最激烈的时刻之一。

As they waited for food, the apes touched, embraced and sometimes kissed one another. Those with the most reassuring physical interactions were more likely to feed peacefully alongside others.

在等待食物时，这些类人猿会彼此接触、拥抱，有时还会亲吻。那些在进食前进行较多安抚性身体接触的个体，更有可能与同伴一起和睦地进食。

The researchers believe this behaviour may date back at least seven million years, suggesting that using touch to build trust and cooperation is an ancient social skill shared by humans and great apes alike.

研究人员认为，这种行为或能追溯到至少 700 万年前，表明通过肢体接触来建立信任和合作关系是人类和大型类人猿共同拥有的一项古老的社交技能。

词汇表

familiar 熟悉的 ，了解的
huddle 聚在一起，围成一圈
bonobos 倭黑猩猩
sanctuaries 动物庇护所，保护区
competitive 竞争激烈的
embraced 拥抱了
reassuring 令人感到安心的，具有安抚作用的
physical interactions 肢体互动，身体接触
peacefully 和睦地，平静地
behaviour 行为
cooperation 合作
social skill 社交技能

听力练习

一、听第一遍音频，回答问题。

1. After physical touch, are chimps more competitive or more cooperative?

二、用一分钟阅读下列问题，然后听第二遍音频并回答问题。

1. Chimps and bonobos behave similarly to human athletes.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

2. The apes studied live in a protected environment.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

3. The apes were seen to fight before eating.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

4. Researchers believe that apes have learnt these skills recently.
a. True
b. False
c. Not given

三、听第三遍音频，将句子补充完整。（提示：可以反复听，直到听清楚每一个词）

1. Anyone who watches team sports may be familiar with the sight of players ______________ before a big match.

2. As they waited for food, the apes touched, ______________ kissed one another.

答案

一、听第一遍音频，回答问题。

Chimps become more cooperative after physical touch.

二、用一分钟阅读下列问题，然后听第二遍音频并回答问题。

1. a. True. Researchers studying chimpanzees and bonobos in African sanctuaries found our closest ape relatives do something similar before feeding time, one of the most competitive moments in their day.

2. a. True. Researchers studying chimpanzees and bonobos in African sanctuaries found our closest ape relatives do something similar before feeding time, one of the most competitive moments in their day.

3. b. False. As they waited for food, the apes touched, embraced and sometimes kissed one another.

4. b. False. The researchers believe this behaviour may date back at least seven million years suggesting that using touch to build trust and cooperation is an ancient social skill shared by humans and great apes alike.

item.title: World's most expensive dinosaur 世界上成交价最高的恐龙化石
item.description:
一具距今约 6700 万年的霸王龙化石在纽约苏富比拍卖行以 5010 万美元，即 3740 万英镑成交，创下恐龙化石价格的新纪录。

It was initially valued at $30 million, but Gus, as the T-rex has been affectionately named, went for much more after a bidding battle that lasted over 10 minutes. Cassandra Hatton, worldwide head of natural history at Sotheby's, said the price reflected the time to excavate and reconstruct the specimen and its quality.

这具霸王龙化石被亲切地命名为 “格斯”，最初估价为 3000 万美元。然而，在持续十多分钟的激烈竞拍后，其最终成交价远远超过预估价格。苏富比全球自然史业务负责人卡桑德拉·哈顿表示，成交价反映了发掘和复原这件标本所耗费的大量时间，以及标本本身的品质。

Standing at 12.5 feet tall and with more than 60% of the bones recovered, it is one of the most complete specimens of its kind. We are unlikely to find out the identity of the buyer immediately. Time will tell if the dinosaur is coming to a museum near you.

该标本高 12.5 英尺，已发现并回收的骨骼超过整体的 60%，是现存最完整的霸王龙标本之一。我们可能无法立即得知买家的身份。只有时间才能揭晓，这具霸王龙化石未来是否会在你附近的博物馆展出。

item.title: First dinosaur bone from Antarctica found in a drawer 来自南极的首块恐龙骨骼在抽屉中被发现
item.description:
一块在抽屉里被遗忘了整整 40 年、看似毫不起眼的化石，最终被证实是人类在南极洲发现的第一块恐龙骨骼。

The ten-centimetre-wide fossil was unearthed during an expedition to James Ross Island four decades ago.

这块宽约 10 厘米的化石，是在四十年前一次对詹姆斯·罗斯岛的科学考察活动中出土的。

Its discovery was recorded in a field notebook with a tiny sketch of the fossil and a note saying vertebra from a large reptile. But that was as far as the identification went, until the fossil was spotted amongst the thousands of specimens stored at the British Antarctic Survey.

一本野外考察笔记记录了这块化石的发现，里面附有一幅简略的化石手绘草图，并写着这是一种大型爬行动物的椎骨。不过，对这块化石的鉴定工作当时仅止步于此，直到最近，有人在英国南极调查局保存的数千份样本中重新注意到了它。

Its distinctive shape revealed it was part of the tail of a titanosaur, the largest dinosaurs ever to roam the Earth. It dates to 82 million years ago, when Antarctica was very different to how it is today.

它独特的形状显示，这块骨骼属于一只泰坦巨龙的尾部。泰坦巨龙是地球历史上已知体型最大的恐龙。这块化石距今约 8200 万年，当时的南极和它如今的面貌完全不同。

It would have been covered in lush forest, providing ample food for this four-legged, long-necked dinosaur.

那时的南极大陆覆盖着茂密的森林，为这种四足、长颈的巨型恐龙提供了充足的食物来源。

item.title: Famous 11th century tapestry to be housed at the British museum 著名的 11 世纪贝叶挂毯将在大英博物馆展出
item.description:
贝叶挂毯（The Bayeux Tapestry）是一件创作于 11 世纪的刺绣作品，描绘了 1066 年诺曼人征服英格兰的历史事件。这张挂毯平时收藏于法国诺曼底的贝叶博物馆，但现在它将运往英国伦敦的大英博物馆展出。

The masterpiece is being loaned to London while its usual home in northern France undergoes a major renovation. 

由于其位于法国北部的馆藏地即将进行大规模翻修，这件艺术珍品将被借展至伦敦。

Many experts believe the Bayeux Tapestry, which charts a time when Anglo-Saxon dominance was replaced by Norman rule, was made in England. 

贝叶挂毯记录了盎格鲁-撒克逊统治被诺曼取代的历史时期。许多专家认为，这件挂毯是在英格兰制作完成的。

So, the prospect of seeing it on display at the British Museum has sparked huge interest, with more than 80,000 people joining an online queue. 

因此，它即将在大英博物馆展出的消息引发了广泛关注，已经有超过八万人在线排队等候预约参观。

In the coming weeks, the embroidery will be moved in a delicate operation involving a double crate, a lorry and a railway shuttle. Officials have insisted it will be as safe as a baby.

未来几周，这件刺绣作品将经历一段精密而慎重的运输作业。届时，它将被装入双层运输箱，通过卡车和铁路接驳运输。相关负责人强调，它将像婴儿一样得到妥善保护。

item.title: Simpler version of Stonehenge discovered 考古学家发现结构更简单的 “巨石阵”
item.description:
考古学家们相信，他们在距离巨石阵（Stonehenge）约五公里外，发现了一处建造年代更早、结构更简单的巨石阵。

Stonehenge was built to mark the movements of the Sun. The huge stones were placed precisely to line up with the sunrise on the summer solstice and sunset on the winter solstice. 

巨石阵是为了标示出太阳的运动轨迹而建造。这些巨石经过精准排列，与夏至日出的方位和冬至日落的方位相对齐。

The discovery in the nearby village of Bulford was a much more simple construction. All that's left of it are two pits in the ground, about 120 metres apart, which archaeologists believe held large wooden posts. 

而在附近的巴尔福德村发现的这处遗址结构则简单得多。如今，它只剩下了地面上两个相距 120 米的土坑。考古学家们认为，这两个土坑里曾经竖立着大型木柱。

The holes were discovered about 10 years ago, but a new analysis examining how the posts were positioned, with the reconstruction of the ancient landscape, sky and horizon, reveals that they accurately lined upwith the Sun on the solstices.

这两个土坑早在十年前就已被发现，但一项新的分析通过研究木柱的排列方式，并结合对远古时期地形、天空和地平线的重建，发现它们与夏至和冬至时太阳的位置精确对齐。

item.title: What happens when octopuses take over 章鱼 “入侵” 给英国渔民带来新问题
item.description:
海洋研究人员表示，目前在德文和康沃尔海域大量出现的章鱼很可能会 “定居下来”。英国海洋生物协会（Marine Biological Association）的最新研究结果显示，在这场 75 年来规模最大的 “章鱼潮” 中，这一入侵物种已经能够在英国海域成功繁殖。

It's never been easy for fishermen in England's southwest to make a living, but now they face a competitor: around 200,000 octopuses, probably coming from the Mediterranean. Climate change is blamed for this migration, and the animals are apparently gobbling up the crab, lobster and other marine life which many fishermen depend on.

对英格兰西南部的渔民来说，谋生从来都不容易，而如今他们面临新的 “竞争对手”——大约 20 万只可能来自地中海的章鱼。人们将这次章鱼迁徙归咎于气候变化。而这些动物似乎正在大量吞食螃蟹、龙虾以及其它渔民赖以谋生的海洋生物。

A report published on Monday found octopuses spotted further north and in Wales, and said fishermen are having to adapt, hunting for the octopuses themselves. One market town recently saw 100 tonnes of octopus sold in a single day.

一份周一发布的报告指出，在更北部的地区以及威尔士也发现了章鱼的身影。报告还提到，渔民正被迫调整策略，开始转而捕捞章鱼。最近，一个集镇甚至在一天之内售出了 100 吨章鱼。

item.title: Why temperature records are being not only broken but smashed 为何极端高温纪录不仅被打破，而且被大幅刷新
item.description:
如果你现在放眼欧洲西部，就会发现很难找到能够避开高温的地区。

European farmers are still counting the cost of last year's drought, which saw plummeting yields of crops like maize and corn.

欧洲农民们仍在承受去年那场大旱带来的损失，那场干旱导致玉米和谷物类作物的产量骤降。

But France today reported it's already short of water, and the European Environment Agency expects this to become a continent-wide problem. 

而就在今天，法国已经报告出现水资源短缺的消息。欧洲环境署预计，这将演变成一个影响整个欧洲大陆的问题。

Paradoxically, this will also lead to worse flooding as more water evaporates and then eventually falls back to Earth.

看似矛盾的是，干旱还会导致更严重的洪涝，因为更多的水分蒸发后，最终会以降水的形式回到地面。

The agency's report also warns there'll be about 60 days each year so hot they're dangerous, and that European healthcare needs to adapt to cope with consequent rises in cardiovascular and respiratory illness.

该机构的报告还警告称，未来每年将有大约 60 天的高温达到危险水平；欧洲的医疗系统需要做出调整，以应对随之增加的心血管和呼吸系统疾病。

In the longer term, disease carrying insects like the tiger mosquito will thrive in the warmer climate.

从长远来看，白纹伊蚊等携带疾病的昆虫将在更温暖的气候中更加活跃并大量繁殖。

Predictions like this have previously been dismissed as scaremongering, but climate scientists say the changes are actually happening even faster than they expected.

此前，类似的预测曾被斥为危言耸听，但气候科学家们表示，这些变化发生的速度实际上比他们预期的更快。

plummeting 骤降

evaporates 蒸发

听力练习
